title: Tu avatar, antes de entrar
brief: Three responsive entry-menu design alternatives for S1, S2, S4, S5 and S6. Each exposes the approved female/male catalogue, one accessory or none, hair and garment colors, nickname and entry CTA. Inline SVG is explicitly a flat mockup: color and text update live, but catalogue silhouettes and 3D fitting are not simulated. Browser-only retention is explained as intended application behavior; these demos deliberately write no storage and perform no navigation. Changing model resets catalogue selections; color and nickname remain. No body-shape controls or account saving. Existing styles and art direction guide these proposals, not an established design system. Canvas opening and ODD Log updates belong to the parent.

artboards.title: Vestidor dividido
artboards.tradeoff: Recommended: side-by-side preview and complete editing form make comparison and revisiting choices immediate. Native selects keep the menu compact and keyboard-friendly, but hide the full catalogue until opened. Stacks vertically on mobile, so the preview is no longer continuously visible while editing lower fields. More initial information than the other directions.

artboards.title: Tu look, a mano
artboards.tradeoff: A compact, centered card puts the preview above three category buttons with visible radio choices. Less simultaneous information and a shorter editing surface; comparing categories requires switching panels. Buttons use normal Tab/Enter semantics and aria-pressed, not ARIA tab semantics. Selected category remains active on model change. Controls wrap instead of creating horizontal mobile overflow.

artboards.title: Hacelo a tu manera
artboards.tradeoff: Three freely revisitable steps reduce first-visit decision load and put nickname/retention explanation at confirmation. More clicks for returning visitors and less simultaneous overview. Step navigation moves focus to the updated heading. Mobile turns the left rail into a wrapping horizontal step list and keeps natural document scrolling.
